name: pawn_storm_against_kingside_castled_king
description: The side to move has at least two pawns on the files in front of the opponent castled king (f/g/h files for kingside castle), while the opponent has fewer such pawns against the side-to-move king.

MOTIF_NAME = 'pawn_storm_against_kingside_castled_king'
MOTIF_DESCRIPTION = 'The side to move has at least two pawns on the files in front of the opponent castled king (f/g/h files for kingside castle), while the opponent has fewer such pawns against the side-to-move king.'
MOTIF_DESCRIPTION = 'The side to move has at least two pawns on the files in front of the opponent castled king (f/g/h files for kingside castle), while the opponent has fewer such pawns against the side-to-move king.'

def motif(fen: str) -> bool:
    import chess
    board = chess.Board(fen)
    stm = board.turn
    opp = not stm

    # Determine castling side for each king based on rook/king position
    # Kingside castle: king on g-file and rook on f-file or h-file, or just king on g/h files near corner
    # Simpler: if king is on g-file or h-file (files 6,7) and hasn't moved far from back rank, call it kingside
    # Or: king is on files 6-7 and rank is 0 (stm) or 7 (opp) with rook nearby? 
    # Better: detect if king is on its back rank and on files e,f,g,h. If king on e-file with rook on h-file -> kingside potential.
    # Actually, let's just check if opponent king is on kingside (files 6-7) and near back rank.
    
    opp_king_sq = board.king(opp)
    if opp_king_sq is None:
        return False
    stm_king_sq = board.king(stm)
    if stm_king_sq is None:
        return False
        
    opp_king_file = chess.square_file(opp_king_sq)
    opp_king_rank = chess.square_rank(opp_king_sq)
    
    # Check if opponent king is castled kingside: on files f,g,h and on ranks 0-1 or 6-7 (back two ranks)
    # For Opp: if white, back rank is 0; if black, back rank is 7
    if opp == chess.WHITE:
        opp_back_rank = 0
    else:
        opp_back_rank = 7
        
    # Kingside castle: king on g-file (6) or h-file (7), or king on f-file (5) with rook on h-file
    # Simplify: king on files >= 5 (e,f,g,h) and rank within 1 of back rank
    if opp_king_file < 5:  # e-file or less -> not kingside
        return False
    if abs(opp_king_rank - opp_back_rank) > 1:
        return False
        
    # Kingside files in front of opponent king: f, g, h (files 5,6,7) for the opponent's side
    # Pawns on those files for STM, advanced (rank >= 4 for white STM, rank <= 3 for black STM? Actually just count STM pawns on those files)
    # The pawn storm: STM has pawns on the files in front of opponent castled king
    
    # Define the kingside files relative to opponent
    # f,g,h are files 5,6,7 regardless of color
    ks_files = {5, 6, 7}
    
    stm_pawns_on_ks = 0
    for sq in board.pieces(chess.PAWN, stm):
        if chess.square_file(sq) in ks_files:
            stm_pawns_on_ks += 1
            
    if stm_pawns_on_ks < 2:
        return False
        
    # Now check STM king side; is STM castled kingside? If yes, opp should have fewer pawns on those files
    stm_king_file = chess.square_file(stm_king_sq)
    stm_king_rank = chess.square_rank(stm_king_sq)
    if stm == chess.WHITE:
        stm_back_rank = 0
    else:
        stm_back_rank = 7
        
    # If STM is also castled kingside, compare
    stm_ks_castled = (stm_king_file >= 5 and abs(stm_king_rank - stm_back_rank) <= 1)
    
    if stm_ks_castled:
        opp_pawns_on_ks = 0
        for sq in board.pieces(chess.PAWN, opp):
            if chess.square_file(sq) in ks_files:
                opp_pawns_on_ks += 1
        # STM must have more pawns on kingside files than opponent
        if stm_pawns_on_ks <= opp_pawns_on_ks:
            return False
            
    return True
